name: Banaro
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: William Butler 1981, A tentative phonology of Banaro (SIL PNG ms.)
earlier_scan.note: A dedicated phonology exists in the SIL PNG archive; sil.org blocked (not reachable by automated download) so the stress statement could not be read.

sources.citation: OLAC: 'OLAC resources in and about the Banaro language' (www.language-archives.org/language/byz), Internet Archive copy 2022-01-23 (live site unreachable today).
sources.note: Bibliographic only: lists Rosetta Swadesh list, transnewguinea.org, Glottolog, PARADISEC DL2-017 and DL2-030 (Laycock notebooks: wordlists incl. Bakaram dialect), WF3-009 (Foley, 'Abu Adjora Language/Banaro Waran language'), PAMBU-DOC1225 (Thurnwald papers). No Butler manuscript and no SIL archive item for byz.

sources.citation: Laycock, D. C. & J. Z'graggen. 1975. The Sepik-Ramu Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1 (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 731-763. hdl:1885/252975 (open).
sources.note: No Banaro-specific statement; phylum-level phonology list includes only 'lack of complex suprasegmental systems'; Banaro noted as 'somewhat aberrant lexically' within the Ramu Super-Stock.

sources.citation: Barlow, Russell. 2023. A grammar of Ulwa (Papua New Guinea) (Comprehensive Grammar Library 6). Berlin: Language Science Press. (Zenodo 8094859, open).
sources.note: Nothing about Waran/Banaro stress; Waran appears only as a neighbouring Ramu language and loan source (pp. 4, 9-16), citing Butler 1981a/b for word forms. (Its phonology chapter is about Ulwa.)

sources.citation: Killian, Don & Russell Barlow. 2022. Deictic marking in adpositions in Ap Ma and Waran. Linguistic Typology at the Crossroads 2(1): 37-64. doi:10.6092/issn.2785-0943/13575 (open access).
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3 'Waran' states 'nearly all information concerning the language originates from Butler's (1981a) sketch grammar'; all Waran data second-hand from Butler 1981a/b; the word 'stress' does not occur.

sources.citation: SIL PNG Language Resources: Banaro [byz] page (www-01.sil.org/pacific/png/show_lang_entry.asp?id=byz), Internet Archive copy 2015-07-24.
sources.note: Catalogue page only: 'Language resources: Nothing yet available or materials are not yet processed.' (i.e. no Banaro phonology/OPD in the SIL PNG archive as of 2015; current pnglanguages.sil.org and sil.org search pages are could not be reached by automated download (not reachable by automated download) by automated download; the Internet Archive has only a 403 capture of the new page).

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2005. Linguistic prehistory in the Sepik-Ramu basin. In A. Pawley et al. (eds.), Papuan Pasts (Pacific Linguistics 572), 109-144. Canberra. hdl:1885/146735 (open; whole-volume PDF).
sources.note: Nothing; Banaro cited only for pronouns and a few cognates (pp. 125-126).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District (Pacific Linguistics C-19). Canberra: ANU. hdl:1885/146580 (open).
sources.note: Silent for Banaro. Sec. 2.23.33-35 (printed pp. 85-86) gives Banaro/Annaberg-group segmental typology only (prenasalised voiced stops, high central vowel, possible glottal stop). Printed p. 6: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Data from Bingo village.

sources.citation: Butler, William. 1981. Preliminary notes on Banaro grammar. Madang: Pioneer Bible Translators. Unpublished MS, 66 pp. (Glottolog 658990).

sources.note: Companion sketch; may repeat an orthography/stress note; same custodians as the phonology MS.

sources.note: Phonology of Banaro's immediate Ramu neighbour by the main current fieldworker in the area; may contain comparative remarks on Waran prosody and shows what Barlow knows of Butler's MS. Journal is open but its site could not be located without web search.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of the Sepik-Ramu basin and environs. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide, 197-432. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.

sources.note: Most recent survey of Ramu-family languages with phonological notes per family; may report Banaro/Ramu stress second-hand (Foley also has his own Banaro/Abu field materials, PARADISEC WF3-009).

sources.citation: Butler, William. 1981. A tentative phonology of Banaro. Madang: Pioneer Bible Translators. Unpublished MS, 66 pp. (Glottolog 658991; describes Western Banaro of Likan and Klorowom).

sources.note: The only dedicated phonological description of Banaro; a 66-page phonology by a Bible translator will almost certainly contain a suprasegmentals/stress section. Held by Hammarstroem (non-shareable scan) and used by Killian & Barlow 2022 / Barlow 2023; ask PBT PNG, Barlow (MPI-EVA) or Killian for a copy.
